recent_open_items.title: [FLINK-41044][python] Let the Python worker flush its logs before closing the logging server
recent_open_items.body_excerpt:
## What is the purpose of the change

This change fixes a shutdown race that can make `CommonDataStreamTests.test_logging_msg` fail with `external log debug-level msg not found`. The same race can drop application logs outside tests.

Before this change, `WrappedSdkHarnessClient.close()` closes the logging server before the control server. The Python SDK harness sends queued log entries on a background thread and drains the rest in `FnApiLogRecordHandler.close()` after the control stream ends. By then the logging stream is already closed, so entries the worker hasn't sent yet are lost.

## Brief change log

  - Close the control server first, so the Python SDK harness leaves its control loop and drains its log queue.
  - Stop accepting new logging calls and wait up to 1 s per environment for the open logging stream to end, then close the logging server and the remaining resources in their existing order. Entries still queued after 1 s can be lost, as before.

recent_open_items.title: [FLINK-41048][container] Fix MiniClusterJobEntryPointITCase race condition
recent_open_items.body_excerpt:
## What is the purpose of the change

MiniClusterJobEntryPointITCase was picking an available port number, and giving that to the MiniCluster to bind to. This introduced a race condition. In the window between identifying an available port, and starting a MiniCluster to bind to it, something else could grab the port, resulting in a test failure when the MiniCluster failed to start because the port it was trying to use was not free.

## Brief change log

I've changed the minicluster config to use bind port 0 so it chooses a free port by itself. This does add some complexity to the test, because it means I have to go and discover what port it used after it's started to be able to submit queries.

## Verifying this change

This is a fix to an ITCase test. Verified by running it repeatedly in a constrained VM to simulate a constrained CI worker.

recent_open_items.title: Fix duplicate Prometheus recovery-write histogram series
recent_open_items.body_excerpt:
## Summary

With recovery enabled, a single `/metrics` response can contain several `bytewax_partd_write_duration_seconds` samples with the same name and labels but different values. Prometheus can drop the conflicting samples even while reporting `up=1`, leaving misleading recovery-write counts and duration statistics.

Create one recovery-write histogram per recovery graph/worker and share its handle across the execution-metadata, snapshot and frontier writers. This aggregates their observations under the existing metric identity.

## Cause and fix

Each `partd_write` currently obtains `global::meter("dataflow")` and constructs an identical histogram independently. In the pinned OpenTelemetry 0.20.0 implementation, those meters have separate instrument caches. The three writers can therefore expose separate accumulators under identical Prometheus labels.

recent_open_items.title: Expose package version as `bytewax.__version__`
recent_open_items.body_excerpt:
## Description

Adds a top-level `__init__.py` for the `bytewax` package that exposes the installed version as `bytewax.__version__`, read from the package metadata via `importlib.metadata`:

```python
import bytewax
print(bytewax.__version__)
```

This makes it easy to sanity-check which Bytewax build is actually installed and to report the version when filing issues. If the package metadata is unavailable (for example, running from an unbuilt source checkout), `__version__` falls back to `"unknown"` instead of raising.

The `__init__` is intentionally lightweight and does not import any submodules, so importing the package stays cheap and does not pull in the compiled extension.

Also adds a test asserting `bytewax.__version__` matches the installed distribution version, and a changelog entry.

Closes #326

recent_open_items.title: Reduce windowing work and stateful map dispatch overhead
recent_open_items.body_excerpt:
## Summary

Lagging watermarks repeatedly scan buffered events, and overlapping count windows repeat the same updates for each event/window pair. This PR reduces those costs and removes an extra Python dispatch layer from built-in stateful maps.

The two changes below preserve public operator signatures, graph IDs, timestamp tie ordering, late-event handling and recovery snapshot formats. The diff contains library code, correctness tests and a changelog entry. Measurements and diagrams are provided here; benchmark scripts and image/data files are outside this PR's code diff.

**Ordered queues.** Backlogs of at least 1,024 retained entries are promoted from the existing list path into arrival-ordered blocks.
